full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Choudhury, J: The leave petitioner Rakhal Chandra Dev was found guilty and convicted under section 326 of the Penal Code and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and to pay a fine of Tk.600/- in default to suffer simple imprisonment for period of one month by the learned additional District Magistrate, Tangail. The learned 2nd  Court, Additional Sessions Judge, Tangail who heard the appeal in Criminal Appeal No. 99 of 1993 dismissed the appeal on affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence by the learned Additional District Magistrate, Tangail. The learned 2nd Court, Additional Sessions Judge, Tangail who heard the appeal in Criminal. Appeal No. 99 of 1993 dismissed the appeal on affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence by the learned Additional District Magistrate. Being aggrieved he filed the revisional application before the High Court Division being Criminal Revision No. 1092 of 1995. The High Court Division discharged the Rule by modification of the sentence to 1½  years rigorous imprisonment. It was contended before the High Court Division that there was delay of 3 days in lodging the FIR and that the courts below erred in law in not drawing an adverse presumption against the prosecution under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. The High Court Division examined the impugned judgment and found that the informant P.W. 1 an eye witness who fully corroborated the case made out in the FIR and that the defence totally failed to discredit his evidence in any way. P.W.2 was the victim of the assault. P.W.3 was the brother of the Informant was also an eye witness to the occurrence. P.W.4 was an eye witness of the occurrence who also fully corroborated the evidence of P.W.1-3. He was a thoroughly independent and natural witness. P.W.5 was the Residential Medical Officer at Tangail Sadar Hospital who examined and found that the injury of grievous nature and that the victim underwent surgical operation. P.W.6 neighbor was also an eye witness to the occurrence. Having discussed the evidence, the High Court Division found that the prosecution had satisfactorily proved the guilty of accused, the leave petitioner. 

 2. It is contended that some of the charge sheeted witnesses were not examined but this submission was not accepted by the High Court Division for not believing prosecution story who had proved their case by examining material witnesses. The High Court Division rightly held that there was a wrong notion that every charge sheet witness is a material witness and as such all charge sheet witnesses are required to be examined by the prosecution. There is no rule of law nor a rule of prudence to consider each and every charge sheeted witness as a material witness for whose non-examination and adverse presumption has to be drawn against the prosecution unless it can be shown from the evidence that his evidence is of vital importance for proper adjudication of the case. When the prosecution succeeds in proving the guilt of the accused by cogent and reliable evidence, there is no logic in taking the view that prosecution should suffer for non-examination of some charge sheeted wit-nesses. In the instant case it was found that the prosecution had proved its case against the accused, leave petitioner, by most consistent, corroborative overwhelming evidence and therefore the non-examination of some charge sheeted witnesses was a matter of no significance and legal consequence. With regard to the delay in filing the FIR it was satisfactorily explained by the prosecution P.W.3 Balaram Deb that as he remained pre-occupied with the treatment of victim Bashudeb who was in a precarious condition, there was some delay in lodging the FIR. After Bashudeb was declared out of danger they lost no time in lodging the FIR. In these facts and circumstances the Single Bench of the High Court Division was satisfied that the delay in lodging the FIR had been sufficiently and satisfactorily explained and we find the learned courts below committed no illegality in accepting the explanation.
